_schema: CardStorm GOAT Vault editorial roster. This file intentionally carries NO card, comp, value, population, or image data yet - only well-known biographical/editorial fields (name, sport, era, teams, position) plus an editorial hobbyRank/rankReason. hobbyRank is CardStorm's editorial ordering of hobby-icon status/collectibility, not a claim of objective statistical greatest-of-all-time ranking - see _editorialDisclaimer. cards and sources are empty arrays for every player until real, sourced Top-20-card data is researched and added sport-by-sport (see data/goat/CARD_RECORD_SCHEMA.md for the shape those records must follow). Never populate cards/sources with placeholder or estimated data.
_editorialDisclaimer: The GOAT Vault ('All-Time Hobby Icons') is CardStorm's editorial selection of the most collectible/iconic players in each sport's history, not a claim that any specific ordering is an objective statistical fact. Individual card rankings within a player's Top 20 (once populated) represent current hobby market value from legitimate sold-comparable evidence, not asking prices or unsold listings.

players.name: Joe Montana
players.rankReason: Iconic vintage-era QB whose rookie cards are a cornerstone of pre-modern football collecting.

comps.insufficientCompsNote: Single sale, but the defining record for this card: BGS's own Pristine 10 population is 4 with none graded higher, so this is inherently a rarely-traded grade tier, not a frequent-sale market. Reported by Beckett as the highest price ever paid for a professionally graded modern-era football card at the time. Sale date independently confirmed: the Beckett News article itself states the sale closed through Modern Marvels' online auction, which 'began in January and officially ended April 25' 2009 - corroborated by the original Beckett.com article, its 2009-dated blog mirror, and a separate SI.com background piece, not merely inferred from a single blog timestamp. Vintage PSA 10 / standard PSA 9 copies of this same card were also found in this research pass, but with conflicting or undated sale prices ($41,000 vs $48,800 claimed for 'PSA 10' with no reconcilable date, and a PSA 9 sale described only as 'recent' with no specific date) - excluded rather than guessed.

population.source: Beckett (BGS Pristine 10 population as of the original 2009 reporting)

sources.name: The Beckett Blog (2009-06-02 mirror, corroborates original article date/content)
Sports Illustrated (SI.com) - Collector owns unique 1981 Topps Joe Montana rookie card (background corroboration)

players.name: Jerry Rice
players.rankReason: The receiver most consistently cited as the position's greatest, with strong vintage rookie demand.

comps.insufficientCompsNote: Only one specifically dated PSA 10 sale could be confirmed (cllct.com, reporting a sale that closed the Friday before its Oct. 4, 2024 publication). cllct and a later SI.com piece (Nov. 2025) both describe roughly six PSA 10 sales since 2023 averaging near $70,000-$84,000, but individual dates/venues for those other sales were not specific enough to verify, so no 3-sale average is calculated here. PSA 10 pop is extremely scarce (~63 of ~39,000 graded, per cllct), making this one of the most condition-sensitive vintage rookies in the hobby.

population.source: PSA population report, cited via cllct.com

_researchNote: Card records were researched via WebSearch result summaries (this environment has no direct page-fetch access to auction-house or price-guide sites), cross-checked against multiple independent, reputable outlets before being recorded as a comp. Every comp is a single dated sale unless explicitly noted otherwise - no three-sale average is computed unless 3+ distinct dated sales of the same specific card were found. This is the same sourcing-honesty standard used throughout CardStorm (see the 2025 Donruss evidence work in data/checklists/football/2025/).
